Section 11C and Section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992
Appeal lies directly to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) within 45 days
Subject to procedural compliance and judicial review under constitutional writs

items: SEBI can perform search and seizure under Section 11C(8) only after obtaining authorization from the Designated Court in Mumbai.
Appeals against orders of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) can be filed directly in the Supreme Court within 60 days on questions of law.
Cease and Desist proceedings under Section 11D cannot be passed by SEBI in respect of listed public companies unless there are reasonable grounds of market manipulation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI was established as a statutory body under the SEBI Act, 1992 to protect investor interests and regulate the securities market.
Under Section 11C, SEBI has the power to direct any person to investigate the affairs of intermediaries or persons associated with the securities market.
SEBI is vested with powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including summoning witnesses and discovering documents.
SEBI can issue cease-and-desist orders under Section 11D and impose monetary penalties for market manipulation, insider trading, and non-disclosure.
Any person aggrieved by an order of SEBI or an Adjudicating Officer can prefer an appeal to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT).
